A BILL TO BE ENTITLED 1

"§ 18C-1002.  Authorizing pari-mutuel wagering. 13 
(a) Notwithstanding any provision of Article 37 of Chapter 14 of the General Statutes, 14 
pari-mutuel wagering and equipment used as part of pari-mutuel wagering as authorized by this 15 
Article is lawful. All pari-mutuel wagers authorized under this Article shall be placed at a legacy 16 
track or satellite facility controlled by a legacy track operator, a startup track controlled by a 17 
startup track operator, or through an ADW licensee, which includes all legacy track operators 18 
and startup track operators. The pari -mutuel wagering licensee shall comply with all of the 19 
following: 20 
(1) Ensure that the registered player is located within the State, and not present 21 
on Indian lands within the State, when placing any sports wager or pari-mutuel 22 
wager, by utilizing geofencing. 23 
(2) Monitor and block attempts to place unauthorized pari-mutuel wagers. 24 
(b) A license granted under this Article shall meet all of the following requirements: 25 
(1) Be in writing and issued by the Commission. 26 
(2) If applicable, be only for the locations identified in the license. 27 
(3) Contain conditions required by this Article. 28 
(c) This Article does not apply to pari-mutuel wagering conducted exclusively on Indian 29 
lands by an Indian tribe operating in accordance with a Tribal -State gaming compact and 30 
authorized to conduct Class III gaming pursuant to a compact with the State. For purposes of this 31 
Article, pari-mutuel wagering is conducted exclusively on Indian lands only if the individual who 32 
places the pari-mutuel wager is physically present on Indian lands when the pari -mutuel wager 33 
is initiated and received by an Indian tribe operating on the same Indian lands in accordance with 34 
a Tribal-State gaming compact and in conformity with the safe harbor requirements as provided 35 
in 31 U.S.C. § 5362(10)(c). 36 
(d) A pari-mutuel wagering licensee shall not, by virtue of such licensure, be authorized 37 
to accept any pari -mutuel wager if the bettor is registered and authorized to make advanced 38 
deposit wagers and physically present on Indian lands when the pari -mutuel wager is initiated 39 
and received. A pari-mutuel wagering licensee shall be authorized to accept a pari-mutuel wager 40 
only if the registered player placing the pari-mutuel wager is physically present in this State when 41 
the pari-mutuel wager is initiated and received. Each pari -mutuel wagering licensee shall use 42 
geofencing approved by the Commission to ensure compliance with this Article. 43 
(e) Nothing in this Article shall apply to fantasy or simulated games or contests in which 44 
one or more fantasy contest players compete , and winning outcomes reflect the relative 45 
knowledge and skill of the fantasy contest players and are determined predominantly by 46 
accumulated statistical results of the performance of individuals. 47 
(f) Upon request, the Commission or the Department of Revenue has the authority to 48 
give reasonable notice and thereafter  audit any pari -mutuel wagering licensee and any 49 
pari-mutuel wagering device supplier licensee as related to pari-mutuel wagering activities. 50
